questions.question: What must an end-to-end latency budget include?
options: Feature lookup, queueing, inference, policy, and network time
questions.explanation: The caller experiences the complete path, not just the model kernel.

questions.question: For affine quantization, what does the scale represent?
options: The real-value distance between adjacent quantized codes
questions.explanation: Scale maps one integer-code step back into real-value space. A wider represented range usually produces a coarser step.

questions.question: What information can a softened teacher distribution provide that a one-hot label cannot?
options: The exact weights the student must use
questions.explanation: A soft target exposes how the teacher ranks alternatives. It does not prescribe student parameters or guarantee deployment performance.

questions.question: Why does a smaller parameter file not guarantee lower latency?
options: The target backend may lack optimized kernels or insert conversion work
questions.explanation: The exported operator graph, device kernels, memory movement, batching, and runtime decide actual latency.

questions.question: Which statement best separates FlashAttention from approximate attention?
options: It evaluates the same dense attention formula in an IO-aware tiled order
It randomly deletes most attention scores
It replaces softmax with a linear activation
It guarantees bitwise-identical output on every backend
questions.explanation: FlashAttention is exact at the mathematical-operation level. Tiling and online softmax change execution and floating-point order, not the dense attention rule.
